_comment: English label dictionary for the Substack edition. Values never change — only the words. `forbid` lists French fragments that must not survive: if one does, the render fails instead of shipping a half-translated legend.

Before the Fed:
keep room to move

indexChart.title: Oil walked away from everything else
indexChart.note: Every line starts at 100 on the previous Friday's close, so they can be compared directly. Oil went one way and stocks, gold and bonds went the other. Note the last step: oil gave some of it back on Friday. ETF prices, distributions excluded.

sectorChart.title: Eleven US sectors, one week
sectorChart.note: Same closes for all of them: energy first, health care last, with technology and communications in between. Energy leading while eight sectors fall is a supply story. The shape is a growth-and-energy barbell, not a defensive rotation.

macroChart.title: The week is stacked on Wednesday
macroChart.note: A count of releases and speeches confirmed by official calendars, with no weighting for how big each one might be. Wednesday holds retail sales, import/export prices, the Fed decision, the press conference and a housing report after the bell. Jobless claims come from an aggregated calendar and are left out. A calendar change breaks this count.

metalChart.title: Same meeting, very different starting points
metalChart.note: One week of returns, measured over the same window for all eight names. This is where each one starts from, not a forecast of how it reacts. Nvidia lost 5.2% and Exxon gained 4.1% in the same five sessions. If these names stop moving through the channels described, the whole propagation idea is wrong.

allocationChart.title: A contango curve, like almost every week
allocationChart.note: Implied volatility rises with maturity: that is the market's normal state, in annualised terms rather than an expected move. What actually moved is the ratio between the short and the one-month point, week over week. An inversion — the short end above the long — would be a genuine change of regime.

decisionChart.title: What would have to happen before adding risk
decisionChart.note: A decision map, not a portfolio: no weights, no probabilities. Stocks and bonds confirming together is what reopens the question of adding; a split keeps the decision on hold. Rebuild this map if the Fed's message differs from the central case.

focusChart.title: The options cost more than the floor is worth
focusChart.note: For each stock: on the left, the gap between Friday's close and the 52-week low; on the right, the move the options price for Friday 18 September. A right bar taller than the left one means a reaction of the size being paid for takes out the yearly floor. A cheaper premium, or a rally before Tuesday, closes that gap.

shortChart.title: Share of selling volume reported away from the main order book
shortChart.note: A month of sessions, not a week. Lennar has held a high band all month: Friday's reading is elevated without being a break, and a shorter window would have manufactured an acceleration that isn't there. Trip.com does the opposite and falls back toward the bottom of its own range. A durable exit from either band changes the reading.
